claims.text: The initial catalyst consists of nanoscale, equimolar PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution nanoparticles.
Ru is an oxophilic element in the proposed catalyst.
Increasing Ru concentration relative to the equimolar composition modifies the local surface electronic structure through ligand effects.
Ru enrichment shifts the local Pt d-band center downward.
A downward shift of the Pt d-band center weakens adsorption of poisoning ethanol-oxidation intermediates such as CO.
Weaker adsorption facilitates desorption or further oxidation of poisoning intermediates.
Reduced intermediate poisoning enhances ethanol-oxidation activity.
A catalyst enriched in Ru by approximately 10% relative to the equimolar baseline will have a more negative ethanol-oxidation onset potential.
The Ru-enriched catalyst will produce higher ethanol-oxidation current densities than the equimolar catalyst under identical conditions.
Operando spectroscopy will detect a measurable downward shift in the Pt d-band center after Ru enrichment.
The Ru-enriched catalyst will have lower surface coverage of poisoning intermediates such as CO.
The proposed mechanism should hold for composition variations within approximately ±20% of the equimolar ratios.
The proposed mechanism should operate under typical aqueous acidic ethanol-oxidation conditions.
The proposed mechanism should operate under typical aqueous alkaline ethanol-oxidation conditions.
The quantitative relationships among Ru enrichment, Pt d-band-center shift, and activity improvement have not been determined.
The equimolar catalyst tested under identical electrochemical conditions is the experimental baseline.
Failure to observe a downward Pt d-band shift, a more negative onset potential, or a higher current density is specified as falsifying the proposed mechanism.
